Berlin police say officers later located the suspect, who reportedly threatened them with a weapon before being shot dead. Authorities say the suspect had previous criminal convictions.

The incident has also renewed concerns about public security and fears that extremist groups could seek to exploit the tragedy for political purposes.

Al Jazeera's Rebecca Collard reports from Berlin.

author: Al Jazeera English
description: More than 360,000 people have been evacuated from their homes and holiday spots as wildfires rage across France and Spain. In France's southwestern Gironde region, 55,000 people were evacuated overnight on Sunday, with some 250,000 people evacuated from the region so far. Around 42,000 hectares of land in Gironde alone have already burned in one of the largest wildfires France has endured since the Second World War. The flames are advancing towards the famous wine-growing port city of Bordeaux. Spain has declared a national emergency, with more than 116,000 people evacuated due to fires west of Madrid and in the eastern Valencia region. Firefighters there found an elderly man dead inside his car on Saturday. French authorities have deployed 1,500 military personnel, 1,700 security personnel, and 1,400 firefighters, with military planes dropping flame retardants. The European Union has dispatched five aircraft and two helicopters to France. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has warn

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The Sudanese military says it has regained full control of a major highway linking Khartoum with el-Obeid, a city that has been under siege by the rival paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF). 
The capture of the Al-Sadirat highway will help the military move troops, weapons, fuel, and supplies, and hinder the RSF's push to seize el-Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan state. 
Half a million people are trapped in the city and have been coming under intense RSF drone attacks, with the United Nations warning of an impending humanitarian catastrophe. 
The highway, a major strategic route, will also ease economic pressure by allowing livestock and agricultural crops to reach markets in the capital, and will enable humanitarian groups to reach displaced families more safely. 
If the route is consolidated, the military could intensify fighting toward the Darfur region, where the RSF holds strongholds. 

Al Jazeera's Almigdad Alruhaid reports from the Sudanese capital, Khartoum.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
This episode examines how mass violence in Darfur has been constructed over time and why many activists, governments and courts have labelled it genocide, even as that term remains politically contested. It traces how environmental stress, neglect of the peripheries and competition over land fed grievances between communities. It shows how Khartoum armed and mobilised militias, how racialised language framed “Arabs” and “Africans” as enemies and how aerial bombing, burning of villages and mass displacement became tools of policy. 

Through survivors’ testimony and legal analysis, the film follows the path from counterinsurgency to crimes against humanity and alleged genocide and asks what justice has - and has not - been delivered for Darfur.

#darfur #sudan #sudanwar #civilwar #politics #africa #documentary #explained
title: Has Darfur descended into genocide? | Al Jazeera Untangles

description:
Flavio Bolsonaro has officially launched his campaign for Brazil’s presidency, seeking to unite the conservative movement once led by his father, former President Jair Bolsonaro.

The senator launched his campaign in São Paulo with support from international right-wing figures, including Argentine President Javier Milei and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Milei attended the event and praised Bolsonaro’s political movement while calling for a shift away from left-wing policies.

Flavio Bolsonaro is attempting to maintain his family’s influence in Brazilian politics after Jair Bolsonaro was barred from running for office. However, the campaign faces major challenges, including legal controversies and competition from current President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

Brazil’s upcoming election is expected to shape the future direction of the country and influence wider political trends across Latin America.

Demonstrators criticised the country's economic conditions and called for democratic reforms, accusing the government of concentrating power in the presidency. Since 2021, Saied has introduced a new constitution, ruled by decree and significantly reduced the powers of parliament.

Opposition figures and civil society groups say the demonstrations are aimed at holding the government accountable and demanding political and economic change.

The protests come as Tunisia continues to face economic challenges and political divisions over the future of its democratic institutions.
